ledger.x: 1198: Přemysl Ottokar I raises Bohemia to a kingdom.
1251: Ottokar II is acclaimed Duke of Austria.
1252 (year bridged): Ottokar occupies Styria.
1 May 1254: Ottokar cedes Styria.
July 1260: Ottokar II defeats Béla IV at Kressenbrunn and wins Styria.
Between 1253 and 1262: the Ascanian margraves obtain Budissin Land.
1266: Ottokar II occupies the Egerland.
1269: Ottokar II inherits Carinthia and Carniola.
1272: Ottokar II acquires Friuli.
November 1276: Ottokar II gives up Austria and its neighbours to Rudolf of Habsburg.
November 1276: Friuli goes.
1277: the Egerland leaves Bohemian hands.
1289: the Duke of Bytom submits to Bohemia.
1290: Kłodzko Land falls back to Bohemia.
1291: Wenceslaus II receives the Duchy of Kraków.
1300: Wenceslaus II takes Greater Poland and Kuyavia and is crowned King of Poland.
By the end of 1305: Władysław the Elbow-high holds Kuyavia again.
Early 1306: Władysław the Elbow-high takes Kraków.
1306: Henry III of Głogów takes Greater Poland.
December 1310: the Luxembourg dynasty takes the Bohemian crown after the Přemyslids die out (Wenceslaus III, 1306).
1319: John of Bohemia gains Upper Lusatia (Bautzen).
1322: Louis IV pledges the Egerland to John of Bohemia.
1327: the Duke of Wrocław becomes John's vassal.
1327: the Duke of Opole becomes John's vassal ('The dukes of Wrocław and Opole became vassals of John').
1329: five more Silesian dukes become John's vassals.
ledger.cp: Silesian duchies of Legnica, Żagań, Oleśnica, Ścinawa and Brzeg

ledger.x: 1329: Görlitz joins Upper Lusatia.
1331: John annexes the Duchy of Głogów.
24 November 1335: Henry VI of Wrocław dies and the vassalage ends.
24 November 1335: the Duchy of Wrocław passes to the Bohemian crown on Henry VI's death (see the vassal_end).
1336: the Duchy of Ziębice (Münsterberg) becomes John's vassal ('1336: Ziębice/Münsterberg was vassalized').
1342: the Duchy of Nysa (Neisse) becomes a Bohemian vassal ('1342: Nysa/Neisse was vassalized').
1348: Silesia is attached to the Crown of Bohemia.
1348: Silesia is attached to the Crown of Bohemia.
ledger.cp: Silesian duchies of Legnica, Żagań, Oleśnica, Ścinawa and Brzeg

ledger.x: 1348: Silesia is attached to the Crown of Bohemia.
1348: Silesia is attached to the Crown of Bohemia.
1348: bridge for the end of the Bytom tint.
7 April 1348: Charles IV sets up the Crown of Bohemia.
1349: John Henry becomes Margrave of Moravia.
1355: Charles IV incorporates the Upper Palatinate (Sulzbach).
1367: Charles IV acquires Lower Lusatia.
1373: Charles IV buys Brandenburg and attaches it to the Crown.
1392: the Duchy of Jawor falls to Bohemia.
1401: Bohemia loses the Upper Palatinate.
1411: Frederick of Hohenzollern gets Brandenburg.
1419: Moravia is held by the King of Bohemia himself.
1437: the Habsburgs take the Bohemian crown.
1445: Brandenburg acquires Cottbus from Bohemia.
1458: the estates elect George of Poděbrady, a Bohemian nobleman.
1468: Matthias Corvinus invades.
1471: the Jagiellons take the Bohemian crown.
21 July 1478: Matthias and Vladislaus ratify the peace at Olomouc.
21 July 1478: Matthias keeps Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia.
1490: Matthias dies and Vladislaus takes back the crown lands.
1526: the Bohemian Diet elects Ferdinand of Habsburg and Bohemia passes to the Habsburg Monarchy.

wars.name: Ottokar II and Béla IV of Hungary over Styria (Kressenbrunn)
wars.outcome: Ottokar defeated Béla IV at Kressenbrunn in July 1260 and 'Béla now ceded Styria back to Ottokar'.

wars.name: Ottokar II against Rudolf of Habsburg (to the Battle on the Marchfeld)
wars.outcome: Rudolf was chosen king in 1273, placed Ottokar under the Imperial ban in 1275 and forced the November 1276 treaty giving up Austria and the neighbouring duchies; Ottokar was defeated and killed at the Marchfeld on 26 August 1278.

wars.name: Bohemian rule in Poland, 1300-1306 (Wenceslaus II and III against Władysław the Elbow-high)
wars.outcome: Wenceslaus II occupied Greater Poland and Kujavia in early 1300 and was crowned at Gniezno on 25 July 1300; Władysław Łokietek captured Kraków in early 1306 and Wenceslaus III was murdered on 4 August 1306 before he could invade.

wars.name: Wenceslaus III's claim to Hungary
wars.outcome: Wenceslaus III was crowned at Székesfehérvár on 27 August 1301 but 'the Kingdom of Hungary was split into several de facto principalities'; his father took him home in August 1304 and he handed the Holy Crown to Otto of Bavaria at Brno on 9 October 1305.

wars.name: Polish-Teutonic War (1326-1332)
wars.outcome: John 'backed the Teutonic Knights'; the page gives no outcome for the war itself.

wars.name: Bohemian-Polish dispute over Silesia and the Polish crown (to the Treaty of Trentschin)
wars.outcome: The Silesian dukes became John's vassals 1327-1342; at Trentschin on 24 August 1335 John waived the Polish crown and Casimir III renounced Silesia in perpetuity, reaffirmed by the Treaty of Namslau in 1348.

wars.name: Hussite Wars
wars.outcome: Crusades in 1420, 1421, 1422, 1427 and 1431 failed; after Pankrác (1 November 1420) 'almost all Bohemia fell into the hands of the Hussites'; the Taborites were beaten at Lipany on 30 May 1434 and Sigismund signed the Compacts at Jihlava on 5 July 1436.

wars.name: Bohemian-Hungarian War (1468-1478)
wars.outcome: Matthias 'conquered Moravia, Silesia, and Lusatia, but he could not occupy Bohemia proper'; 'In 1478, the war ended following the treaties of Brno and the Olomouc' (peace ratified 21 July 1478); Matthias kept the three lands until his death in 1490.

certainty.note: None of the pages describes a boundary; the Bohemian mountain ring, the Austrian and Styrian acquisitions of 1251-1276 and the Polish claims of 1291-1306 are all approximate.
The Silesian-Polish frontier is sharp after the Treaty of Trentschin (24 August 1335): 'a border that remained stable and in effect until after World War I'.
